title: I shipped a mobile game as a solo dev with AI doing most of the heavy lifting. Here’s my workflow (and a difficulty question)
author: patxy01
selftext:
I’m a solo dev and I just released the open beta of **Flip Flap the Giraffe** on Android: an endless runner where you steer a giraffe’s **head** and **body** independently, one thumb each. It started as an old French joke about a giraffe and a helicopter. 🦒🚁

AI was involved in almost every part of the pipeline, so here’s how I split the work between me and the machines:

**🧠 Code: Claude Code (Unity / C#)**  
I write specs, make design decisions and review; the agent implements, writes tests and runs them headless. The project has a layered architecture (simulation / infrastructure / presentation) with 550+ automated tests, which turned out to be key: the agent can’t break things silently when every change has to pass the suite.

**🎨 Art: InvokeAI (SDXL), locally**  
Backgrounds, decor and characters generated in a consistent style, then cleaned up and cut out with scripts. The hardest part wasn’t generating; it was keeping a coherent art direction across 3 worlds.

**🎵 Audio: Stable Audio + ACE-Step, locally**  
Music loops and sound effects, mixed with small Python tools.

**🌍 Localization, store assets, trailers**  
Full English translation with a key-based system plus consistency tests; Play Store screenshots and promo videos rendered **by code** from the real game, so I can regenerate them in any language after every UI change.

**What I’d tell anyone starting:**  
• Tests + clear architecture rules = the agent stays on rails.  
• You’re still the game designer: AI is great at “how”, terrible at deciding “what’s fun”.  
• Keep every asset reproducible (scripts, not one-off prompts).

**Now my question:** after hundreds of runs, I think the game is too easy, but my first testers died within seconds. If you have an Android phone, I’d love your **best distance** \+ **too easy / just right / too hard**. Link in the comments.

Happy to answer questions about the workflow!
